topicName: Handling Imbalanced Data: Class Weights and BalancedAccuracy
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Handling Imbalanced Data: Class Weights and BalancedAccuracy in Scikit-learn"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Class imbalance occurs when one class significantly outnumbers the other in a dataset. This is common in domains like fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and churn prediction. Standard machine learning models often optimize for overall accuracy, predicting the majority class while failing to detect the minority class. This tutorial explores how to use class weights and balanced accuracy in Scikit-learn to build robust models."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Problem with Standard Accuracy"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Imagine a dataset with 99 percent negative cases and 1 percent positive cases. A naive model that always predicts the negative class achieves 99 percent accuracy, yet it is completely useless for identifying the positive class. Standard metrics like accuracy or ROC-AUC can be misleading when classes are skewed."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Class Weights"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Many Scikit-learn classifiers accept a parameter called class_weight. Setting class_weight='balanced' tells the algorithm to inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data. The model penalizes misclassifications of the minority class more heavily during training."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# Generate synthetic imbalanced data
X, y = make_classification(n_samples=1000, weights=[0.95, 0.05], random_state=42)

# Initialize model with balanced class weights
model = LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced', random_state=42)
model.fit(X, y)"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Evaluating with Balanced Accuracy"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"When evaluating models on imbalanced data, standard accuracy is insufficient. Scikit-learn provides balanced_accuracy_score, which computes the average of recall obtained on each class. For binary classification, it is the average of sensitivity (true positive rate) and specificity (true negative rate)."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.metrics import balanced_accuracy_score, accuracy_score

y_pred = model.predict(X)

print('Standard Accuracy:', accuracy_score(y, y_pred))
print('Balanced Accuracy:', balanced_accuracy_score(y, y_pred))"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always split your data into train and test sets before applying class weights or evaluating metrics to prevent data leakage."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Combine class weights with robust evaluation metrics such as balanced accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Experiment with custom dictionaries for class_weight if automated balancing does not yield optimal decision thresholds."}]
